forecaster_note: A day of small clean surf with breezy offshore winds — best suited for cruising bigger boards. Friday brings a long-period SSE swell with clean offshore winds early before northerlies develop. Saturday drops back a bit, but some small to fun surf, staying clean all day. Sunday picks up again, though maybe not until the winds trend onshore. Monday looks fun-sized and clean in the morning before strong onshores and building size. — Surfline forecast team, Sydney

wind.summary: NW 18 km/h gusting 42 at 9am, swinging WSW 20 km/h by midday — offshore the whole day, but gusty enough to put texture back into the face. No onshore at any point.

shark.summary: SharkSmart NSW live: no shark detections or drone sightings at Dee Why, Long Reef, Curl Curl or Manly in the last 24 h. The only genuine Northern Beaches sighting was a drone spot at Avalon Beach at 4:09pm yesterday (water evacuated) — about 14 h ago and 13 km north of your spots. Feed is healthy: 15 real statewide detections in the last 24 h, the most recent a tagged shark at Lighthouse Beach, Ballina at 1:32am today.

days.label: Today
days.note: Small and clean, but thin. Energy peaks at just 73 kJ and the primary is 2.1ft @ 12s from 172° — dead south, the exact angle the Dee Why bay shadows. Long Reef and Curl Curl convert it to a rideable 2–3ft and hold Fair through 9am; Dee Why and Manly get the leftovers at 1–2ft. Consistency is a full 100/100, so sets keep coming — they are just knee-to-thigh. Wind is offshore all day (NW 324° then WSW) but gusting 42 km/h at 9am. Tide pushes to a 1.55m high at 12:24pm, so your 10am–12pm window is on the fill. Verdict: a longboard or mid-length cruise at Long Reef, or save yourself for tomorrow.

tip.text: The 1.2ft @ 10s from 79° sits right in your 30–80° sweet spot and is the only swell here with the right angle — it is just too small to carry a session. Frontside rights at the Point need size and a north-of-east angle; today has neither. Long Reef is the same water with better exposure.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: This is the day. A long-period S groundswell fills in overnight — 5.2ft @ 11s from 185° — and energy jumps from 73 kJ today to 190 kJ average, peaking at 422. Wind is almost nothing: 9 km/h W offshore at 9am, then a 4 km/h E sea breeze by midday, which is barely a breath. Everything holds Fair through the mid-morning. The catch is the same as always: 185° is dead south, so Long Reef (4–6ft, chest to overhead) and Curl Curl (4–5ft) will out-perform Dee Why (3–4ft), and Manly stays shadowed at 2–3ft. Consistency 93/100. Your 10am–12pm window is dead centre of the best conditions. If you can only surf once this week, surf Friday.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: A tale of two days. Saturday is the throwaway — dropping to 1–3ft with energy back to 60–86 kJ and a nasty W/NW offshore building to 30 km/h gusting 62 by midday. Long Reef and Curl Curl still scratch a Fair rating early; Dee Why and Manly go Poor. Then Sunday flips: the morning is quiet (1–3ft, 84 kJ at 9am), and from midday a long-period S groundswell lands — 6.9ft @ 12s from 185° — with energy exploding to 1,077 kJ by 3pm and 1,212 by 6pm. Long Reef and Curl Curl go 6–8ft, Dee Why 4–6ft, Manly stays 2–3ft. Two problems: 185° is dead south so Dee Why is shadowed again, and the wind swings ESE onshore 12–16 km/h from midday, right as it fills. Consistency drops to 87. The honest read: Sunday afternoon is the biggest surf on the chart in weeks but it arrives outside your window and slightly onshore. Monday 7 Sep looks the smarter play — fun-sized and clean in the morning before strong onshores.
